scope: Simultaneous full fixed-j=1 collisions at adjacent fixed-M parameter points p and p+2
proved: The exact phase neighbor is (h,s,p,M)->(h-4,s+3,p+2,M) for h>=5.
If both rows collide, then [p(p+2)]^2 divides gcd(C0(M),C1(M)).
This square product is already a subproduct of Item197/264's distinct-collision-prime square radical and gives no extra valuation copy.
After exact rational pullback, the mixed state solution module is ker(A mod p) x ker(B mod p+2).
For ranks r_p,r_q in {0,1,2}, the mixed solution count is p^(4-r_p)(p+2)^(4-r_q); every rank-drop branch is retained.
CRT idempotent row blocks have determinant e_p^2 e_q^2 det([A;B])=0 modulo p(p+2), regardless of rational transversality.
Integer row scaling instead contributes the tautological factor [p(p+2)]^2 to the stacked determinant.
A transverse determinant-one model with X=(p,0,p+2,0) proves that cross-field transversality forces no p(p+2)-divisibility of state coordinates.
Item275's actual pair (5,1,p=29,M=21)->(1,4,p=31,M=21) is rationally transverse but remains split between different fields.
For twin primes p,p+2 with p>5, both p-2 and p+4 are composite by reduction modulo 3, so neighboring edges do not overlap in the actual range.
The classical Brun/Selberg upper-bound sieve gives O(M/log^2 M) neighboring prime edges and O(M/log M)=o(M) endpoint prime-log weight.
Even a perfect exclusion of every neighboring double collision would affect zero linear mass.
Item149 already books the first post-Cartier copy; the full fixed-j=1 raw ceiling remains 1/36 per 6M.
